name: Duskwell Mood Gels — Focus Slate
description: Smooth, matte grey gel capsules containing Duskwell's proprietary nootropic-adjacent compound blend — designed to reduce ambient anxiety while sharpening attentional focus without stimulant jitter. A BCI-compatible formulation with a mild black sesame and smoked honey flavor.
flavor_profile: Subtle, earthy black sesame with a thin veil of smoked honey — understated, almost medicinal, intentionally not sweet
cultural_context: Favored by Tier 3 knowledge workers and Tier 4 executives who need sustained cognitive performance without the social stigma of pharmaceutical use. Positioned as a 'wellness product' rather than a drug, which keeps it in a regulatory gray zone that Duskwell's legal team actively maintains. BCI users report slightly enhanced mesh interface clarity during the gel's active window.
story_hooks: A Tier 4 corporate board is secretly requiring executives to use Duskwell Focus Slate before quarterly negotiations — an employee leaks this as a coercion complaint, arguing they were pressured to use a bioactive substance.

Duskwell's proprietary compound has an undisclosed interaction with a specific third-generation BCI implant model — users experience involuntary memory consolidation, essentially recording experiences with unusual clarity they didn't consent to.

A Tier 1 chemistry student reverse-engineers Focus Slate and begins selling a crude approximation at Φ1.50 a dose in the Shelf — attracting both desperate buyers and dangerous attention from Duskwell's asset protection division.
